# dsh-seeker-os

**A complete system engineering project built on top of DeepSeek Harness**

Turn DSH into a personal AI operating system: execution dashboard · interactive cards · Bot team / group chat / voice · memory · profiles · skills · sync · end-side encrypted roaming

## What is this

DeepSeek Harness is the foundation, and dsh-seeker-os is a complete system engineering suite built on top of it. It consolidates the host's conversations, tools, memory, profiles, skills, connectors, sync, and multi-Bot orchestration into one coherent personal AI operating system. **It doesn't just show you what the AI is actually doing.** It also gathers scattered capabilities like memory, profiles, and skills into a set of workbenches, and lets Bots collaborate, report, and do scheduled work like colleagues.

| What you care about | After installing |
|---|---|
| You want to know what the AI did, but don't want to see a screen full of tool logs | A right-column dual-pane execution dashboard, with tool calls rendered in plain language |
| You want it to give you something clickable directly | **HTML cards** in the response (real JS runs) and **iu native interactive cards** (sliders / tables / checklists / boards / weather / market quotes / links, 15 types in total) |
| You want it to draw an architecture or flow diagram | Hand-written inline SVG, rendered directly in the conversation flow |
| You want a whole AI team | A main Bot + sub-Bots + **group chat** (members can actually see each other's context) + diaries + voice calls |
| You want the AI to remember your preferences | Workbench **memory** (isolated by owner, so Bots don't mix up each other's) |
| You want to store account passwords, cards, and IDs, and have them automatically enter the context | Workbench **profiles** (encrypted on the end side; plaintext never enters the model context) |
| You don't want to set everything up again when switching computers | **Sync settings**: memory / profiles / skills / MCP / keys are end-side encrypted and pushed to your private GitHub repo |

## Installation

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:Kr-ATG/dsh-seeker-os
```

Videos you saved but never watched, and web pages you meant to read: let AI read them for you, organize them, and pick out the ones really worth your time.

Videos and web pages you've saved, MoonDigest helps you read through with AI and organize. Your data stays in your browser; nothing goes to the author's servers.

1. Install from the [Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/bnjihpbocpimaipifanfkjjpfdbigggd).
2. Settings → 'AI Platforms' → '+ Add platform', choose a preset, enter your API key, and click 'Test connection'. When the browser asks whether it may access this address, click Allow. Settings save automatically when changed; there is no Save button. Supports DeepSeek, Zhipu GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, OpenRouter, and any OpenAI-compatible API. You can add several and switch in the sidebar under 'Select AI platform'; the triage desk's AI also uses the platform selected here.
3. Log in to Bilibili. Bilibili only shows subtitles (including AI subtitles) to logged-in users, and the triage desk also requires login to read your favorites folders.
4. Open a Bilibili or YouTube video and click **✦ AI Summary** in the extension's icon menu.

Buttons marked ✦ call AI and use your own API quota; other buttons do not. Without AI configured, you can still view and download subtitles, use focus mode, export notes, and triage manually.

**Read**
- View Bilibili and YouTube subtitles (human-made, AI, auto-generated); copy or download as SRT or TXT. When there are no subtitles, AI summarizes using the description and top comments.
- AI sidebar: summarize videos or web pages, then ask follow-up questions. On ordinary web pages, first use requires clicking 'Allow page reading' (Chrome will request access to read all websites).
- Focus mode: video on the left, subtitles on the right, scrolling as the video plays; click a line to jump to it.

**Triage** (Bilibili only)
- Triage desk: AI first looks at titles, then reads subtitles, and tells you whether each video in your favorites is worth keeping, can be cleared, or is uncertain; you then keep or unfavorite. **Unfavoriting really removes it on Bilibili**; press U to undo. See the [triage guide](https://github.com/PathGao/MoonDigest/blob/HEAD/docs/TRIAGE.md).
- Tag videos and uploaders; tags also appear on Bilibili pages. AI judgments appear on Bilibili pages only if enabled in Settings → 'Bilibili Triage Desk'.
- Watch progress (off by default): shows on covers how much you have watched and whether you have finished.

**Record**
- Write a one-line note on a video. AI chats are saved by video and web page into 'Digest Records', where you can search them and add stars and tags. Starred chats are not deleted by 'Clear all AI chats' and do not count toward the chat limit.
- Export Markdown, or write to Obsidian (optional; the settings page has setup instructions).

[Simplified Chinese](https://github.com/Sadami3066/DeepDeep/blob/HEAD/README.md) · [English](https://github.com/Sadami3066/DeepDeep/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)

[Overview](#概览) · [Feature Preview](#功能预览) · [UI Showcase](#ui-展示) · [Quick Start](#快速开始) · [Installation & Configuration](#安装与配置) · [Development](#开发与构建) · [Documentation](#文档与反馈) · [Contributing](#贡献) · [License](#license)

## Overview

DeepDeep is designed to match the built-in assistants on all phone manufacturers. It supports waking up with a long press of the power button, and floating voice input and output.

It also comes with a complete Harness engineering setup, including tools, skills, long-term memory, MCP extensions, and a plugin system. It runs conveniently on your phone, with no server and no computer that must stay on. You can open it anytime, anywhere. Long-press the power button, say one sentence, and it starts working to get things done.

DeepDeep includes a built-in ultra-lightweight Linux environment that can cover 99% of desktop office and coding tasks. It essentially runs on the Android system, and it can also work with your phone's files: finding images, cleaning up junk, organizing files, writing code, optimizing the phone, and even opening a virtual screen through screen tools to operate your apps.

In addition, DeepDeep has a rich plugin ecosystem. It can connect to external services through MCP and CLI to help with remote tasks, including Feishu, WeCom, AMap, McDonald's MCP, Notion notes, email, and more, to improve efficiency in work, life, and study.

Finally, DeepDeep follows open-source principles. Its code is secure and transparent, with no external network services other than the LLM requests you send to your model provider, and it performs no data collection or uploading at any point.

When using DeepDeep, please follow the user agreement in the app.

The current version is 1.0.3. Installation packages are published on [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Sadami3066/DeepDeep/releases), and the source code is public.

# dsh-rewind DeepSeek Harness plugin: **one-click in-place rewind of the conversation to any earlier user message**.
Done within the same window, with no new branch and no window switch, and it can restore workspace files as well. This is Claude Code-style `/rewind` semantics. [English](https://github.com/SiriLee/dsh-rewind/blob/HEAD/README.en.md) | Chinese Deliberately focused and kept minimal, it does one thing: **rewind in place to any distant user message**, and it can **also restore the files you edited** along the way. - **In-place message rewind**: the target message and everything after it are withdrawn from both the **model context** and the **rendered conversation**, and the target message text is automatically refilled into the input box. It always completes within the original session, with no new branch and no leftover copies. - **Lightweight backup and restore**: aligned with Claude Code. It tracks files edited by write-type tools and restores them on rewind, and it can also restore external changes to tracked files. **Partial tracking, backup before write, and unchanged files are not stored.** It does not depend on git. - **Safety guarantees**: session logs are append-only for rewind markers and are never edited or deleted. File backup and restore are security-hardened. **Thorough tests** are maintained long-term alongside DSH upgrades. # PNC Nav2 — 3D Navigation Planning and Control System

A 3D navigation system for wheel-legged robots, focused on **Planning & Control**, with hot-swappable plugin-based algorithms.

This repository is a personal learning and practice project maintained independently, and it may be open-sourced later. It depends only on the official ROS 2 Jazzy, Gazebo Harmonic (`ros_gz`), and basic Nav2 packages (`map_server` / lifecycle_manager). It does not depend on any third-party robot product SDK, deb packages, or private environment scripts.

## ✨ Features

- **Plugin architecture**: global planning, local planning, and path tracking can all be hot-swapped via pluginlib
- **Implemented algorithms**: A* 2D, RRT*, Pure Pursuit, Stanley, DWA (still being refined)
- **Real map integration**: supports the OccupancyGrid published by `map_server` (includes `maps/111`)
- **Incremental development**: 2D differential-drive vehicle validation → 3D quadruped robot dog → real-robot deployment
- **Simulation stack**: Gazebo Sim Harmonic (playground + simple differential-drive vehicle) + Unitree Go2 (3D, planned)

```
Navigation layer (NavServer)
  ├─ Global Planner (plugin) → AStar2D / RRTStar
  ├─ Path Tracker (plugin)   → PurePursuit / Stanley
  └─ Local Planner (plugin)  → DWA (Phase 2)
         │
Motion layer (cmd_vel → robot control)
         │
Platform layer (Gazebo Sim / real hardware)
```

lizi600jin/dsh-ensp.body:
# dsh-ensp

An automation tool for Huawei eNSP. It generates topologies, starts devices, pushes configuration in order, and verifies the result after each command.

It provides three invocation methods that share the same core:

- CLI: suited to scripted batch operations
- MCP Server: connects to clients such as Claude Desktop and Cursor
- DeepSeek Harness plugin: used inside a session as a model tool

## Features

### Generating topologies

Generates `.topo` files that eNSP can open and display correctly. Supports built-in scenarios, as well as custom devices and links.

Device models and interface layouts are defined in `src/core/models.mjs`, covering 16 models. When parsing a topology, port names are taken first from the `<interface>` blocks declared by the device itself. The same model may have a different port layout after an extension card is installed, so the declared block is the only reliable basis.

```js
import { twoPcLab, writeTopology } from 'dsh-ensp'

await writeTopology('lab.topo', twoPcLab({ vlan: 10 }))
```

```js
import { buildTopology, autoLayout } from 'dsh-ensp'

const topo = autoLayout(
  buildTopology()
    .add('R1', 'AR2220', { x: 180, y: 120 })
    .add('R2', 'AR2220', { x: 460, y: 260 })
    .link('R1', 'GigabitEthernet0/0/0', 'R2', 'GigabitEthernet0/0/0')
    .finish()
)
```

Several constraints in the topology format come from eNSP itself: interface groups must match the model, and link anchors must fall within the icon's bounding box. If any of these is wrong, eNSP opens a blank canvas without reporting an error. For the rules, see [`docs/ENSP-FORMAT.md`](https://github.com/lizi600jin/dsh-ensp/blob/HEAD/docs/ENSP-FORMAT.md).

### Starting and stopping devices

Toolbar buttons are located automatically, so no manual clicking is needed. After startup, each device is confirmed ready one by one, then the window is minimized so the desktop remains usable.

```bash
ensp probe          # recalibrate button positions
ensp up lab.topo    # open, start, confirm ready, minimize
ensp stop           # close all devices
```

eNSP allows only one instance to run at a time. After an abnormal exit, a zombie process that does not hold a thread may remain. It keeps holding the single-instance lock, so the next launch opens only a blank window. Before starting, the tool identifies and cleans up such processes.

# dsh-plugin-shop-accounts

**Centrally manage login sessions for six e-commerce back offices: log in once, reuse long-term, check on a schedule, and auto-fill when signed out.**

Account management plugin for DSH Desktop. Each store maps to its own independent login profile, and listing and scraping scripts reuse the same login session directly, so no repeated logins are needed.

[功能特性](#功能特性) · [支持平台](#支持的平台) · [安装](#安装) · [快速开始](#快速开始) · [数据存放](#数据存放位置) · [安全机制](#安全机制) · [支持与交流](#支持与交流) · [更新日志](https://github.com/monagisa/dsh-plugin-shop-accounts/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md)

---

## Why it's needed

Login sessions on e-commerce back offices are the most fragile link in automated workflows:

- One machine must manage multiple stores at once. Cookies from different platforms overwrite each other, and browser windows compete for focus.
- Taobao-family `cookie2` / `_tb_token_` cookies are session-level: they are discarded when the window closes, so the next visit lands on the login page again.
- Once a session expires, a manual QR scan or CAPTCHA is required, and listing, scraping, and reporting tasks all stall at login.
- Listing and scraping scripts each maintain their own login state, so every new platform means logging in again.

This plugin's job is **to maintain login state only**. Each store gets one independent profile. After a one-time login, the plugin handles detection, renewal, and automatic credential fill. Script-side code only needs to read profile information (the ego profile, or the Chrome debugging port) to reuse it. The plugin does not list products, change prices, or submit orders.

---

### Login state management

| Capability | Description |
| --- | --- |
| One profile per store | Each store has its own profile, and cookies are not shared. The ego backend uses one profile and one TaskSpace per store. The Chrome backend uses one `user-data-dir` and one fixed debugging port per store. |
| Login in a real window | Launches a headed browser. The user completes QR scans, passwords, and slider verification in the real window. The plugin polls login state in the background and, once login succeeds, writes the login state to the profile when "Done" is clicked. |
| Silent detection | Probes login state and writes it back without disturbing the window. The Chrome backend uses a headless instance (about 2.6–3.1 seconds per store). The ego backend opens a temporary space under the same profile, reads cookies read-only, and closes it immediately. |
| Auto-fill on logout | When a password is saved and the login method is "password auto-fill", opening the store or a scheduled check that finds a login page fills in the form and submits it automatically. Failure reasons are classified and shown. Wrong credentials pause automatic retries for that store. |

## Why dsh-suite

DSH launched without an official plugin registry. Today, finding plugins means digging through GitHub's `dsh-plugin` topic (50+ scattered small plugins) and a handful of static awesome-lists that pop up daily. Meanwhile, DSH itself keeps shipping **breaking changes**.

wynter-yaxley/atrium-desktop.body:
Keep the way Windows works, swap in liquid glass with real-time refraction,
and use one design language to tie the taskbar, Start menu, control center, notifications, and widgets into a single whole. ## More than desktop beautification Windows' desktop is layers of several generations of design: the taskbar, tray, Start menu, notifications, and quick settings each have their own corner radii, font sizes, and animations. Atrium redoes the layer you see every day, without changing how you use Windows. - **Usage unchanged**: pinning apps, switching windows, right-click menus, and dragging files onto app icons to open them all work as before. - **Same glass**: the bar, panels, menus, notifications, and widgets use the same material, reflecting the desktop behind them in real time. - **Same design language**: corner radii, spacing, fonts, and animations follow one set of rules, so the same control feels the same everywhere. - **Three independent modules**: the taskbar, desktop widgets, and stage manager can each be turned on separately; using just one is fine. - **Chinese and English UI**: in the Settings Center, "System → Language" lets you choose Simplified Chinese, English, or follow Windows; the bar, panels, menus, notifications, widgets, and Settings Center all switch together. - **Clean**: it injects no code into system processes, modifies no system files, installs no services, and requires no administrator privileges. After you exit, Windows' own taskbar comes back as usual. ## Features ### Liquid and frosted The glass refracts the image behind it, with a bit of highlight and dispersion at the edges. For clarity, use liquid (left); for calm, use frosted (right). Transparency, blur, and refraction strength can also be adjusted in the Settings Center. Text on the glass automatically switches to dark or light depending on the brightness behind it. ### Taskbar - A capsule-shaped glass bar floats at the bottom of the screen. When the pointer passes over it, icons swell like waves, and pausing shows the app name. - Hovering over an open app shows a live preview of each of its windows, which you can switch to or close directly. - Right-clicking an icon, as with the Windows taskbar, lists the program's own jump list: pinned and recent files, folders, workspaces, and tasks the program provides (such as a browser's new window or private window). You can also run as administrator and view properties. It can be turned off in the Settings Center to restore the simple menu. - Pinned apps can be reordered by dragging. When a foreground app is fullscreen or maximized, the bar steps aside (it can also be set to always stay visible or always stay hidden). When a fullscreen app such as a game or video is in the foreground, moving the pointer to the bottom edge does not summon the taskbar, just like the Windows taskbar, so fullscreen games are not pushed back to the desktop. Once open, Win + 1…9 can launch the apps on the bar directly. - Multi-monitor: pausing at the bottom edge of another screen summons the Dock; it can also be pinned to the primary screen or a specified screen, or shown on all screens. On the "Displays" page of the Settings Center, you can choose whether taskbar apps appear on all screens, on the primary screen and the window's screen, or only on the window's screen, and adjust the cross-screen dwell time. - Widgets and stage manager can each be assigned a desktop display separately. zzNaLogiczz/chher-public.body:
## Reading and Discussion

Read reviews, go through long threads, follow replies, and share your own experience. Chher organizes its interface around these everyday actions, keeping content and ongoing discussions in view.

### Long posts, read continuously

Read the body text continuously, tap images to view them, follow links to the site directly, and play Bilibili videos within the app. Portal reviews and forum posts can both be browsed in familiar ways.

### Replies, follow the conversation

Comments can be grouped by quote relationships, you can switch back to the original floor, or view only the original poster's posts. Replies within a thread expand in place, quotes support jumping, and long discussions are easier to follow.

### From reading to participating

Replies, new posts, article comments, and private messages are all completed within the app. Image attachments support compressed uploads, and edits are kept as drafts. When a captcha appears, you can switch to the original site's web page to continue.

| Entry | What you can do |
| --- | --- |
| **Featured** | Browse portal highlights, reviews, news flashes, and the community's latest and popular discussions |
| **Sections** | Find content by section, filter sections, collapse pinned posts, search posts |
| **Messages** | View notifications, read and reply to private messages |
| **Me** | Access your profile page, your posts, favorites, points, and badges |
| **Original page** | Open the corresponding original site page at any time and continue using web features |
| **App updates** | View release notes, resume downloading the installer, verify it, and hand it to the system for installation |

## Quick Start

Currently supports **Android 7.0 and above**. The development environment uses Flutter **3.44.2**, Dart **3.12.2**, JDK **17**, and the Android SDK.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/zzNaLogiczz/chher-public.git
cd chher-public
flutter pub get
flutter run
```

When multiple devices are connected, first run `flutter devices`, then specify the target device with `flutter run -d <设备ID>`. For normal development, debug signing is sufficient.

First prepare your own Android signing key, then copy the configuration example:

```sh
cp android/key.properties.example android/key.properties
```

Fill in the keystore path, alias, and password in `android/key.properties`, then build:

```sh
tool/build_release.sh 1.0.10             # Generate a universal package containing all supported architectures
```

The installation package is located at `build/release/1.0.10/chher-1.0.10.apk` and includes ARM64, ARMv7, and x86_64. Both new and old clients fetch the universal package, so there is no need to group them by the original package type.

Native libraries are packaged with compression, and debug symbols are stored separately in `symbols/` in the same directory. Maintainers should keep them so crash logs can be resolved. Version number...
